Gershon
gûr'shŏn
n. (eldest son of Levi, and the Levitical family charged with the curtains and coverings of the tabernacle — the carriers of the fabric of the house of God)
From Hebrew Gershon or Gershom, probably from garash, to drive out or expel — the same root behind the name Moses gave his own son, “a stranger in a strange land”. The gentilic is Gershonite.

Biblical Definition

Gershon was the firstborn of Levi — “and the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari” (Gen 46:11) — and gave his name to one of the three Levitical divisions that carried the tabernacle through the wilderness. The division of labour is exact and it is worth attending to. Kohath, the second son, carried the holy things: the ark, the table, the candlestick, the altars, borne on the shoulder and never touched. Merari carried the frame: boards, bars, pillars, sockets, and the wagons for them. And “the charge of the sons of Gershon in the tabernacle of the congregation shall be the tabernacle, and the tent, the covering thereof, and the hanging for the door” (Num 3:25) — the curtains, the coverings of rams' skins and badgers' skins, the hangings of the court, the cords. Their commission is summarised in six words: “This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, to serve, and for burdens” (Num 4:24). They were the oldest branch and they were given the cloth, not the gold; two covered wagons and four oxen; and they pitched behind the tabernacle westward. Under David the Gershonites appear among the singers and over the treasures of the house of the LORD.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Gershon; in sacred history he is the eldest son of Levi, from whom the Gershonites, one of the three great Levitical families, are named.

expand to see more

GERSHON, n. The eldest son of Levi, also written Gershom; the name is thought to signify expulsion or a stranger.

From him descended the Gershonites, one of the three families of the tribe of Levi.

Their charge in the wilderness was the tabernacle and the tent, the coverings, hangings and cords.

They were given two wagons and four oxen for the carriage of their burden, and pitched westward behind the tabernacle.

In the days of David certain of the Gershonites were set over the treasures of the house of the Lord.

Gen 46:11 — "And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari."

Exo 6:16 — "And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations; Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi were an hundred thirty and seven years."

Num 3:25 — "And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the tabernacle of the congregation shall be the tabernacle, and the tent, the covering thereof, and the hanging for the door of the tabernacle of the congregation,"

Num 4:24 — "This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, to serve, and for burdens:"

Modern Corruption

Assigned, unglamorous service is treated as a lesser calling; the eldest son of Levi was given the curtains, and Scripture records his charge in the same breath and the same detail as the ark.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the doctrine of appointed service. Gershon was Levi's firstborn and did not get the ark; a younger brother's house carried the holy things on their shoulders while Gershon's house folded curtains onto wagons. Nothing in the text treats this as a demotion. The Holy Ghost specifies the badgers' skins and the cords with the same seriousness as the mercy seat, because in the worship of God the question is never how visible the office is but whether the man is doing the thing appointed to him. Paul argues it at length in 1Co 12, and gives the conclusion: “God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him” (1Co 12:18).

The second lesson is in the phrase “to serve, and for burdens.” Levitical work was heavy, unromantic, physical labour: hauling wet skins, coiling cords, loading oxen, and doing it again at the next encampment. The New Testament keeps the register — deacons, helps, governments, bearing one another's burdens. A congregation that can only recruit for the visible ministries and cannot find men to carry the coverings has misunderstood what the house of God has always required.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Gershon / Gershom (H1648, H1647), from garash (H1644), to drive out; mishkan (H4908), tabernacle; massa' (H4853), a burden.

expand to see more

Hebrew Gershon (H1648) — Gershon; the firstborn of Levi, ancestor of the Gershonites.

Hebrew garash (H1644) — to drive out, expel; the likely root, sounding the theme of sojourn.

Hebrew mishkan (H4908) — the tabernacle, a dwelling place; the fabric structure in Gershon's charge.

Hebrew 'ohel (H168) — the tent; the goats' hair covering spread over the tabernacle.

Hebrew massa' (H4853) — a burden, that which is lifted; the word of Num 4:24, service defined as load-bearing.

Usage

"“The sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari” — the three divisions of the sanctuary's service."

"“The tabernacle, and the tent, the covering thereof” — a charge itemised by God."

"“To serve, and for burdens” — the whole commission in six words."
